gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each all-NVMe box draws at idle for each M.2 slot, or what that comes to per year. From named reviewers' wall-meter idle readings: Asustor Flashstor 6 Gen2 is 13.1 W ÷ 6 = 2.2 W per slot (115 kWh/yr), TerraMaster F8 SSD Plus is 19.7 W ÷ 8 = 2.5 W per slot (173 kWh/yr) and UGREEN DXP480T Plus is 18 W ÷ 4 = 4.5 W per slot (158 kWh/yr).
standout_why: I compared against computingforgeeks.com (cited), homelabcompass.com (cited) and starryhope.com (top result). ComputingForGeeks already converts PCIe lanes to GB/s and compares each slot with a 10GbE port. It also prices a fully loaded box. StarryHope gives SSD $/TB. None of the three gives idle watts per box or per M.2 slot, or yearly kWh. None works out the price per slot either.
decides: This adds to the pick rather than changing it. For an always-on box, the Flashstor 6 Gen2 has the lowest idle draw per slot and per year, even with six slots on Gen4 lanes. The F8 SSD Plus gives the most slots for little more power per slot. But each slot is Gen3 x1, so one drive can't fill 10GbE (1.25 ÷ 0.985 = 1.27, so at least two drives striped). The DXP480T Plus costs about twice as much idle power per slot as the other two. You get the i5 and Thunderbolt for that. The three reviewers used different drive setups, so the per-slot figures are a guide, not a ranking from one lab.

findings.value: 1× Gen4 x4, 3× Gen4 x2, 2× Gen4 x1 = 12 Gen4 lanes ≈ 23.6 GB/s, about 19× one 10GbE port
findings.note: Asustor lists the per-slot lanes. 4 + 3×2 + 2×1 = 12 lanes; 12 × 1.969 GB/s per Gen4 lane (the per-lane figure ComputingForGeeks uses) = 23.6 GB/s; 23.6 ÷ 1.25 GB/s (10 Gb/s ÷ 8) = 18.9. Asustor's own rating is 17.9 W in operation and 1.2 W asleep, with a 90 W adapter.
